tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an economics class.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: How bad economic policies can affect private businesses
options.B: How psychology affects the economic decisions we make
options.C: How avoiding economic losses is more important than making economic gains
options.D: How traditional economics helps individuals maximize utility

questions.stem: According to the speaker, one problem with traditional economics is that it

options.A: accepts the biases and emotions of ordinary people
options.B: forgets that losing money is painful and getting it is pleasurable
options.C: favors rational people over those who aim to maximize their benefit
options.D: assumes that people will always act in a way that maximizes their utility

questions.stem: Which of the following situations might be due to loss aversion?

options.A: Holding on to an unwise investment for too long
options.B: Guarding against bias and emotionally motivated choices
options.C: Choosing a familiar brand over a new one
options.D: Making policy based on theory rather than on actual behavior

questions.stem: What does the concept of "anchoring" refer to in behavioral economics?

options.A: When someone focuses too heavily on making financial gains
options.B: When someone relies too much on an initial piece of information
options.C: When someone accepts the very first offer in a negotiation
options.D: When someone becomes too preoccupied with examining their biases

tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: A historical overview of Einstein's contributions to physics
options.B: An overview of the development of modern computing
options.C: A concept that reshapes our understanding of physical laws
options.D: A debate about the speed of light and its limitations

questions.stem: According to the talk, what happens when two particles are entangled?

options.A: They begin spinning in the same direction.
options.C: A property of one particle can tell us about a property of the other.
options.D: The particles merge into a single particle.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention "spooky action at a distance"?

options.A: To quote Einstein's reaction to quantum entanglement
options.B: To explain how particles communicate faster than light
options.C: To describe a modern experiment that proved Einstein's theory
options.D: To introduce a term now used in quantum computing design

questions.stem: Why was Einstein skeptical about quantum entanglement?

options.A: It was believed to be a temporary effect that wouldn't last.
options.B: It appeared to violate a fundamental principle of physics.
options.C: It was assumed to occur only under extreme conditions.
options.D: It was thought to contain a mathematical error.

tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a history podcast.

questions.stem: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

options.A: The complexities of ancient sea travel
options.B: How the Silk Road influenced modern transportation networks
options.C: The importance of the Maritime Silk Road
options.D: The spread of silk during the Han Dynasty

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about the name "Silk Road"?

options.A: It was first used in ancient Chinese maps.
options.B: It suggests how precious silk was in ancient times.
options.C: It is just one of the many names people use for it.
options.D: It is misleading since the Silk Road was actually a network of routes.

questions.stem: What do the two cities mentioned in the talk have in common?

options.A: Their advantageous locations by the sea

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention the monsoon?

options.A: To suggest that most merchants preferred traveling by camel caravan
options.B: To explain the benefits of predictable wind cycles
options.C: To compare weather patterns in inland and coastal cities
options.D: To explain the decline of ancient trade between China and India
